items.meaning: Indicates that the audio quality of the other person's voice is poor and intermittent.
items.example: I'm sorry, but you're breaking up quite badly; I can't hear what you're saying.
items.plain: I can't hear you clearly because your audio is cutting in and out.
items.note: Common informal phrase for poor call quality. Can be used in both personal and professional contexts.

items.meaning: Expresses that the connection is failing, and the other person's voice is becoming inaudible.
items.example: Oh dear, I think I'm losing you; the signal here is terrible.
items.plain: The connection is bad, and I can no longer hear you clearly.
items.note: A polite way to indicate a failing connection. Suitable for most situations.

items.meaning: Describes an intermittent connection where parts of the conversation are missed.
items.example: I keep missing words because the line is cutting out every few seconds.
items.plain: Your voice keeps disappearing, making it hard to understand you.
items.note: Slightly more formal than 'breaking up', often used for phone calls rather than video.

items.meaning: Informs someone that their video feed has stopped moving on a video call.
items.example: Just to let you know, your video is frozen, so we can't see you moving.
items.plain: Your picture on the video call has stopped moving.
items.note: Direct and practical for video calls. Neutral tone.

items.text: the connection is a bit patchy
items.form: the connection is a bit patchy
items.meaning: Suggests that the internet or phone signal is inconsistent and unreliable.
items.example: I apologize if I cut out; the connection is a bit patchy where I am today.
items.plain: My internet signal is not very strong or consistent right now.
items.note: A polite and slightly understated way to describe a poor connection. Common in professional settings.

items.meaning: Asks if the other person can hear clearly, often after a connection issue or starting a call.
items.example: Hello? Can you hear me alright, or is the audio still a problem?
items.plain: Are you able to hear my voice clearly?
items.note: A standard check for audio quality. 'Alright' is common in spoken English.

items.meaning: Promises to redial immediately, usually after a dropped call or connection issue.
items.example: It seems we've lost the connection; I'll call you right back.
items.plain: Our call ended unexpectedly, so I will phone you again immediately.
items.note: A common and reassuring phrase when a call drops. Implies urgency.

items.meaning: Explains that one's internet service is not functioning correctly or reliably.
items.example: I'm sorry for the delay, my internet is acting up again this morning.
items.plain: My internet connection is not working properly at the moment.
items.note: Informal but widely understood. Used to explain technical difficulties.

items.meaning: Suggests restarting the call or video session to improve connection quality.
items.example: Since the audio is so bad, let me try reconnecting to see if that helps.
items.plain: I will end this call and start it again to fix the sound.
items.note: A proactive suggestion to resolve connection issues. Professional and polite.

items.meaning: Asks if the other person is still on the call, often after a period of silence or connection trouble.
items.example: Hello? Are you still there? I haven't heard anything for a moment.
items.plain: Have you remained on the call, or did we get disconnected?
items.note: A common question when silence occurs unexpectedly on a call. Neutral tone.

items.meaning: Indicates that the other person's voice is very quiet or indistinct.
items.example: Could you speak up a little? I can barely hear you over the background noise.
items.plain: Your voice is very quiet, and it's difficult for me to understand you.
items.note: Direct but polite way to request the other person to speak louder or clearer.

items.meaning: Describes distorted audio that is muffled and unclear, as if speaking from a distance.
items.example: I'm afraid it sounds like you're underwater; the audio is very distorted.
items.plain: Your voice is muffled and unclear, making it hard to understand.
items.note: An idiomatic and vivid description of poor audio quality. Informal but widely understood.

items.meaning: Notes that the call repeatedly disconnects or experiences severe interruptions.
items.example: This is frustrating; we keep losing each other, maybe we should try another platform.
items.plain: Our call keeps disconnecting, which is making communication difficult.
items.note: Expresses shared frustration over persistent connection problems. Informal.

items.meaning: Explains that the wireless or cellular reception is poor, causing connection issues.
items.example: I'm in an area where the signal is weak, so I might drop off unexpectedly.
items.plain: The phone or internet reception here is not strong, so the call might end.
items.note: A common explanation for poor call quality, especially on mobile phones. Neutral.

items.meaning: Politely states that one cannot hear the other person clearly.
items.example: I'm having trouble hearing you; could you perhaps move closer to your microphone?
items.plain: It is difficult for me to hear what you are saying.
items.note: A polite and common way to address audio issues without blaming the other person.

items.meaning: Informs the other person that one's own voice is intermittently disappearing.
items.example: Please bear with me if my audio is cutting out; I'm having some technical issues.
items.plain: My sound is intermittently stopping, so you might miss some words.
items.note: Useful for self-diagnosis of connection problems. Professional and clear.

items.meaning: Indicates that the other person's video or entire connection is temporarily stopping.
items.example: I think you're freezing up again; your picture isn't moving at all.
items.plain: Your video is stopping and starting, or your connection is pausing.
items.note: Common for video calls. Similar to 'your video is frozen' but implies a temporary state.

items.meaning: Describes audio that is intermittent and unclear, making speech difficult to understand.
items.example: I'm sorry, but the sound is breaking up quite badly on your end.
items.plain: Your audio is not clear and keeps cutting out.
items.note: A common and clear way to describe poor audio quality. Neutral tone.

items.text: may I just jump in here
items.form: May I just jump in here
items.meaning: A polite way to ask for permission to interrupt and contribute to the conversation.
items.example: May I just jump in here with a quick point about the budget?
items.plain: Could I interrupt briefly to add something?
items.note: Polite and slightly informal, used to interject without being rude. Common in meetings.

items.meaning: A formal and polite way to ask for a moment to interrupt and make a point.
items.example: If I could just interject for a moment, I have a slightly different perspective.
items.plain: May I interrupt briefly to share my thoughts?
items.note: More formal than 'jump in'. Used to politely assert one's turn in a discussion.

items.text: to circle back to your point
items.form: To circle back to your point
items.meaning: Indicates a return to a previously mentioned topic or idea in the conversation.
items.example: To circle back to your point about the timeline, I think we need more flexibility.
items.plain: Returning to what you said earlier about the timeline, I have a thought.
items.note: Professional and useful for managing discussion flow, ensuring all points are addressed.

items.text: I just wanted to add that
items.form: I just wanted to add that
items.meaning: Introduces an additional piece of information or a supplementary comment.
items.example: Before we move on, I just wanted to add that the client seemed very pleased.
items.plain: I would like to include this extra piece of information.
items.note: A common and polite way to contribute to a conversation, often after someone else has spoken.

items.meaning: Prompts the other person to continue speaking after an interruption or pause.
items.example: Sorry, I interrupted you. You were saying about the new project?
items.plain: Please continue speaking about what you were discussing.
items.note: A polite way to hand the conversational turn back to someone. Neutral tone.

items.meaning: Gives permission to the other person to speak and assures them of attention.
items.example: Please, go ahead, I'm listening intently to your proposal.
items.plain: You can speak now; I am paying attention to what you say.
items.note: Encouraging and polite, often used when someone hesitates to speak.

items.meaning: Indicates a willingness to wait for the other person to complete their thought before speaking.
items.example: I have a question, but I'll let you finish your explanation first.
items.plain: I will wait for you to complete your statement before I speak.
items.note: A polite way to manage turn-taking, showing respect for the other speaker.

items.meaning: A polite apology before breaking into someone else's speech to make a point.
items.example: Sorry to interrupt, but we're running short on time for this agenda item.
items.plain: I apologize for breaking in, however, I need to say something.
items.note: A standard polite interruption. Essential for maintaining good conversational etiquette.

items.text: did you want to add anything
items.form: Did you want to add anything
items.meaning: Invites the other person to contribute further to the discussion.
items.example: Before we conclude this topic, did you want to add anything, Sarah?
items.plain: Do you have any further comments or points to make?
items.note: A polite way to ensure everyone has a chance to speak. Inclusive.

items.text: I'll hand it over to you
items.form: I'll hand it over to you
items.meaning: Indicates that one is finished speaking and is passing the turn to another person.
items.example: That's all from my side for now, so I'll hand it over to you, Mark.
items.plain: I have finished speaking, and now it is your turn to talk.
items.note: Common in presentations or structured discussions to transition speakers. Professional.

items.meaning: A concise way to indicate that it is now the other person's turn to speak.
items.example: I've finished my update, so over to you for the next section.
items.plain: I am done speaking, so you may begin.
items.note: More informal than 'I'll hand it over to you', but still professional. Direct.

items.meaning: Indicates a temporary stop in one's speech, inviting questions or comments.
items.example: I'll pause there and see if anyone has any immediate questions.
items.plain: I will stop speaking now to allow for questions or comments.
items.note: Useful for managing the flow of a presentation or detailed explanation. Professional.

items.text: what are your thoughts on that
items.form: What are your thoughts on that
items.meaning: Asks for the other person's opinion or perspective on a specific matter.
items.example: I've shared my view, so what are your thoughts on that particular issue?
items.plain: What is your opinion about that specific topic?
items.note: An open-ended question to encourage discussion and gather feedback. Professional.

items.meaning: Offers to provide more details or a fuller explanation if needed.
items.example: If that wasn't clear, I'm happy to elaborate further on the proposal.
items.plain: I can give you more details if you need them.
items.note: Polite and helpful, showing willingness to clarify. Professional.

items.meaning: Introduces an attempt to make something clearer or correct a misunderstanding.
items.example: Before we proceed, let me just clarify the exact terms of the agreement.
items.plain: I want to make sure this point is clear and understood correctly.
items.note: A common phrase for ensuring accuracy and avoiding misinterpretation. Professional.

items.meaning: Signals a transition to a new topic, inviting final comments on the current one.
items.example: Before we move on to the next agenda item, are there any other points?
items.plain: Are there any final comments before we discuss the next topic?
items.note: Useful for structuring discussions and ensuring all points are covered. Professional.

items.text: just to pick up on that
items.form: Just to pick up on that
items.meaning: Introduces a comment that builds upon or refers back to something previously said.
items.example: Just to pick up on that point about the budget, I think we have some flexibility.
items.plain: Referring back to what you just said, I have a related comment.
items.note: A smooth way to link one's contribution to a previous speaker's point. Professional.

items.meaning: Expresses a desire to contribute one's opinion or perspective to a discussion.
items.example: If I may, I'd like to weigh in on the discussion about the new policy.
items.plain: I would like to share my opinion on this topic.
items.note: Polite and professional, indicating a desire to contribute meaningfully.

items.text: perhaps I could offer a perspective
items.form: Perhaps I could offer a perspective
items.meaning: A very polite and humble way to introduce one's opinion or viewpoint.
items.example: Perhaps I could offer a perspective on how this might impact our international team.
items.plain: May I share my view on this matter?
items.note: Highly diplomatic and formal, used to introduce a potentially differing opinion gently.

items.meaning: Promises to speak concisely and not take up too much time.
items.example: I know we're short on time, so I'll keep my comments brief.
items.plain: I will speak for only a short time.
items.note: Polite and considerate, especially in time-sensitive meetings. Professional.

items.meaning: Suggests that all necessary topics have been discussed and the meeting can end.
items.example: Well, I think we've covered everything on the agenda for today.
items.plain: I believe we have discussed all the necessary points.
items.note: A common way to signal the end of a discussion or meeting. Neutral and professional.

items.meaning: Introduces the final part of a discussion or meeting, leading to its conclusion.
items.example: To wrap things up, let's quickly review our action points.
items.plain: To conclude our discussion, let's summarize our decisions.
items.note: A very common and versatile phrase for ending conversations or meetings. Informal to semi-formal.

items.meaning: Politely ends a call, indicating that the other person is free to leave.
items.example: It was good catching up, but I'll let you go now.
items.plain: I will end our call now, so you can continue with your day.
items.note: A polite and common way to end a call, especially when you initiated it. Friendly.

items.text: I won't keep you any longer
items.form: I won't keep you any longer
items.meaning: A polite way to end a conversation, implying respect for the other person's time.
items.example: I think we've addressed all points, so I won't keep you any longer.
items.plain: I will not take up any more of your time.
items.note: Formal and considerate, often used in professional or slightly more formal personal calls.

items.meaning: Expresses pleasure at having spoken to someone, especially after a period of time.
items.example: Thanks for the call, it's been good catching up with you.
items.plain: I enjoyed talking to you and hearing your news.
items.note: A warm and friendly closing, suitable for both personal and professional calls with acquaintances.

items.text: I think that's all for now
items.form: I think that's all for now
items.meaning: Suggests that there are no more immediate topics to discuss, signaling an end.
items.example: Unless anyone has anything else, I think that's all for now.
items.plain: I believe we have finished discussing everything for this moment.
items.note: A polite and common way to conclude a meeting or discussion. Neutral.

items.meaning: States that the allotted time for the call or meeting has expired.
items.example: Unfortunately, we've run out of time, so we'll have to continue this next week.
items.plain: Our scheduled time for this discussion has finished.
items.note: A direct but neutral way to end a meeting due to time constraints. Professional.

items.text: I'll follow up with an email
items.form: I'll follow up with an email
items.meaning: Promises to send an email containing further information or a summary.
items.example: I'll follow up with an email containing the meeting minutes and action points.
items.plain: I will send you an email later with more details.
items.note: A standard professional closing, indicating next steps. Very common.

items.meaning: Suggests having another brief contact or meeting in the near future.
items.example: We've made good progress, so let's touch base again soon to review.
items.plain: Let's talk again briefly sometime in the near future.
items.note: A common professional phrase for scheduling a follow-up. Friendly and proactive.

items.meaning: Promises to contact the other person again at a later time.
items.example: Thanks for the information; I'll be in touch once I have an update.
items.plain: I will contact you again when I have new information.
items.note: A standard and polite closing, implying future communication. Neutral.

items.meaning: Expresses gratitude for the time the other person spent on the call.
items.example: Thanks for your time today; I appreciate you fitting me in.
items.plain: I am grateful that you spent your time speaking with me.
items.note: A polite and professional closing, especially after a scheduled meeting or call.

items.text: I appreciate you taking the call
items.form: I appreciate you taking the call
items.meaning: Expresses gratitude to the other person for accepting and participating in the call.
items.example: I appreciate you taking the call on such short notice.
items.plain: Thank you for accepting and participating in this phone call.
items.note: A polite and professional way to show appreciation, especially if the call was unexpected.

items.text: we should probably call it a day
items.form: we should probably call it a day
items.meaning: Suggests ending the work or discussion for the day.
items.example: It's getting late, so I think we should probably call it a day.
items.plain: It is time for us to stop working or discussing for today.
items.note: Informal and friendly, often used to end a long or tiring session. Common.

items.meaning: Indicates that one has finished speaking on a particular topic or for the call.
items.example: I think that covers my points, so I'll leave it there for now.
items.plain: I have finished making my points on this topic.
items.note: A concise way to conclude one's contribution or the entire call. Neutral.

items.meaning: Asks if there are any remaining topics or questions before concluding.
items.example: Before we hang up, is there anything else we need to discuss?
items.plain: Do you have any other matters to talk about?
items.note: A standard closing question to ensure nothing is overlooked. Neutral.

items.text: I'll get back to you on that
items.form: I'll get back to you on that
items.meaning: Promises to provide an answer or information about a specific query later.
items.example: That's a good question; I'll get back to you on that after I check with the team.
items.plain: I will find the answer to your question and contact you again.
items.note: A common and professional way to defer an answer. Implies a follow-up.

items.meaning: Expresses satisfaction at having made contact or spoken with someone.
items.example: Thank you for the productive discussion; it was good to connect.
items.plain: I enjoyed our conversation and making contact with you.
items.note: A professional and polite closing, especially for initial contacts or business calls.

items.meaning: Promises to transmit the written summary or minutes of the discussion.
items.example: I'll send over the notes from our meeting by the end of the day.
items.plain: I will email you the summary of our discussion.
items.note: A common professional commitment at the end of a meeting. Clear and actionable.

items.text: looking forward to our next chat
items.form: Looking forward to our next chat
items.meaning: Expresses anticipation for a future conversation with the other person.
items.example: This was helpful; looking forward to our next chat about the project.
items.plain: I am eager to speak with you again soon.
items.note: A friendly and positive closing, suitable for ongoing professional or personal relationships.

items.text: I'll let you get back to your day
items.form: I'll let you get back to your day
items.meaning: Politely ends a call, acknowledging the other person's schedule and responsibilities.
items.example: Thanks for your time; I'll let you get back to your day now.
items.plain: I will end our call so you can resume your other activities.
items.note: A considerate and professional way to conclude a call, especially if it ran long.

items.meaning: States the intention to record a message for someone who is unavailable.
items.example: Since she's not available, I'll leave a message with her assistant.
items.plain: I will record or write down information for her.
items.note: A standard phrase when someone is not reachable directly. Neutral.

items.text: please leave a message after the tone
items.form: Please leave a message after the tone
items.meaning: An instruction from an answering machine or voicemail system to record a message.
items.example: You've reached my voicemail; please leave a message after the tone.
items.plain: After you hear the beep, you may record your message.
items.note: A very common phrase heard on voicemail systems. Passive voice.

items.meaning: Promises to call back someone who has previously called and left a message.
items.example: Thanks for calling; I'll return your call as soon as I'm free.
items.plain: I will phone you back because you called me.
items.note: A standard and polite way to acknowledge a missed call and promise a callback. Professional.

items.text: I'm just calling to follow up
items.form: I'm just calling to follow up
items.meaning: Explains the purpose of a call as a check-in or reminder about a previous interaction.
items.example: Hi, I'm just calling to follow up on the email I sent last week.
items.plain: I am phoning you to check on the status of something we discussed earlier.
items.note: A common and polite opening for a follow-up call. Professional.

items.meaning: States the specific subject or reason for making the phone call.
items.example: Good morning, I'm calling in reference to the job application I submitted.
items.plain: I am phoning you about the specific topic of...
items.note: Formal and precise, used to clearly state the purpose of a call. Professional.

items.text: could you pass on a message
items.form: Could you pass on a message
items.meaning: Asks someone to relay information to another person who is unavailable.
items.example: Could you pass on a message to John that I'll be late for the meeting?
items.plain: Would you please tell John this information for me?
items.note: A polite request when speaking to an intermediary. Common in offices.

items.meaning: Promises to transmit the information received to the intended recipient.
items.example: Don't worry, I'll relay the message to her as soon as she gets back.
items.plain: I will deliver your information to the person it is for.
items.note: A professional and reassuring response when taking a message for someone else.

items.text: I'll make sure they get the message
items.form: I'll make sure they get the message
items.meaning: Assures the caller that their information will definitely reach the intended person.
items.example: Yes, I'll make sure they get the message about the revised deadline.
items.plain: I will ensure that the person receives your information.
items.note: A strong assurance that the message will be delivered. Professional and helpful.

items.meaning: Explains the call is a brief check-in, not requiring a lengthy discussion.
items.example: Hi Sarah, I'm just touching base about the project's progress.
items.plain: I am calling for a quick update or check-in.
items.note: Informal but professional, used for brief, non-urgent check-ins. Common.

items.text: I'll give you a call back
items.form: I'll give you a call back
items.meaning: Promises to phone the other person again at a later, more convenient time.
items.example: I'm a bit tied up right now, but I'll give you a call back in an hour.
items.plain: I will phone you again later.
items.note: A common and polite way to end a call or promise a return call. Neutral.

items.meaning: States the name of the person one is attempting to contact by phone.
items.example: Hello, I'm trying to reach Mr. Henderson regarding a delivery.
items.plain: I am attempting to speak with Mr. Henderson.
items.note: A standard and polite opening when calling an organization to speak to a specific person.

items.meaning: Promises to send a short message, usually an email or text, to someone.
items.example: I'll drop them a line to confirm the details of our meeting.
items.plain: I will send them a brief message.
items.note: Informal and friendly, implying a quick, non-urgent communication. Common.

items.meaning: Promises to communicate with someone via electronic mail.
items.example: Instead of calling, I'll send them an email with all the necessary documents.
items.plain: I will contact them by sending an electronic message.
items.note: A direct and common way to promise communication, often preferred over calls for details.

items.text: I'll get them to call you
items.form: I'll get them to call you
items.meaning: Promises to arrange for the intended person to phone the caller.
items.example: She's in a meeting, but I'll get them to call you back as soon as possible.
items.plain: I will ask that person to phone you.
items.note: A common and helpful response when taking a message for someone else. Neutral.

items.meaning: States the purpose of a callback, referring to the original message.
items.example: Hi, this is David. I'm returning your call about the invoice query.
items.plain: I am phoning you back regarding the topic you mentioned in your message.
items.note: A standard and professional opening for a return call. Clear and efficient.

items.text: thanks for getting back to me
items.form: Thanks for getting back to me
items.meaning: Expresses gratitude for someone returning a call or message.
items.example: Thanks for getting back to me so quickly regarding my request.
items.plain: I appreciate you contacting me again in response to my message.
items.note: A polite and common expression of appreciation for a timely response. Neutral.

items.text: I just wanted to check in
items.form: I just wanted to check in
items.meaning: Explains the call is a brief contact to see how things are progressing or if help is needed.
items.example: Hi, I just wanted to check in on how the project was coming along.
items.plain: I am calling simply to see how you are doing or how things are progressing.
items.note: Informal and friendly, used for a quick, non-demanding contact. Common.

items.text: I'll be sure to pass that on
items.form: I'll be sure to pass that on
items.meaning: Assures the caller that their message or information will definitely be relayed.
items.example: Yes, I'll be sure to pass that on to the relevant department.
items.plain: I will certainly make sure that information is given to the correct people.
items.note: A strong and polite assurance that a message will be delivered. Professional.

items.text: I'll let them know you called
items.form: I'll let them know you called
items.meaning: Promises to inform the unavailable person that someone tried to reach them.
items.example: She's not at her desk, but I'll let them know you called.
items.plain: I will tell the person that you phoned them.
items.note: A standard and polite response when someone is unavailable. Neutral.

items.meaning: Promises to deliver the specific information provided by the caller.
items.example: Certainly, I'll give them your message as soon as they're free.
items.plain: I will deliver the information you provided to them.
items.note: A direct and common way to confirm message delivery. Neutral.

items.text: I'll make a note of that
items.form: I'll make a note of that
items.meaning: Promises to write down the information for future reference.
items.example: Thank you for the update; I'll make a note of that for the report.
items.plain: I will write down this information so I don't forget it.
items.note: A professional and reassuring phrase, indicating attention to detail. Common.

items.text: I'll get back to you shortly
items.form: I'll get back to you shortly
items.meaning: Promises to contact the other person again very soon.
items.example: I need to check my calendar, but I'll get back to you shortly with a time.
items.plain: I will contact you again very soon.
items.note: A polite and professional way to promise a quick follow-up. Common.

items.text: I'll be sure to follow up
items.form: I'll be sure to follow up
items.meaning: Assures the other person that one will take the necessary next steps.
items.example: Thanks for raising that; I'll be sure to follow up with the team.
items.plain: I will definitely take the necessary actions regarding this.
items.note: A strong and professional commitment to take action. Reassuring.

items.meaning: Promises to provide regular updates on a situation or development.
items.example: The situation is still evolving, but I'll keep you posted on any changes.
items.plain: I will regularly inform you of new developments.
items.note: Informal but widely used in professional contexts. Friendly and proactive.

items.meaning: Promises to inform the other person about something in the future.
items.example: Once I have the final decision, I'll let you know immediately.
items.plain: I will tell you the information when I have it.
items.note: A very common and versatile phrase for promising future information. Neutral.

items.text: I'll check on that for you
items.form: I'll check on that for you
items.meaning: Promises to investigate or find information on behalf of the other person.
items.example: I'm not sure about that detail, but I'll check on that for you.
items.plain: I will find the information you need.
items.note: A helpful and polite offer to assist. Professional and proactive.

items.meaning: Promises to resolve a problem or organize something efficiently.
items.example: Don't worry about the booking, I'll get that sorted for you by tomorrow.
items.plain: I will arrange or fix that problem for you.
items.note: Common in British English, implies efficiency and resolution. Informal but professional.

items.meaning: Promises to investigate a matter or problem.
items.example: That's an interesting point; I'll look into it further and get back to you.
items.plain: I will investigate that issue.
items.note: A standard professional response when more information or action is required. Neutral.

items.text: I'll make sure to do that
items.form: I'll make sure to do that
items.meaning: Gives a strong assurance that a specific action will be taken.
items.example: Yes, I'll make sure to do that before the end of the day.
items.plain: I will definitely perform that action.
items.note: A firm and reassuring commitment to complete a task. Professional.

items.meaning: Promises to connect the caller to another person or department.
items.example: Certainly, I'll put you through to customer service now.
items.plain: I will connect your call to the correct person or department.
items.note: A standard phrase used by receptionists or operators. Professional.

items.meaning: Indicates willingness to wait on the line while the other person attends to something.
items.example: No problem, I'll hold for a moment while you retrieve the file.
items.plain: I will wait on the phone line for a short time.
items.note: A polite and patient response when asked to wait during a call. Professional.

items.meaning: Promises to return to the call very quickly after a brief absence.
items.example: Just a second, I need to grab a pen; I'll be right back.
items.plain: I will return to the call immediately.
items.note: A common phrase for a very short, temporary interruption. Informal but acceptable.

items.text: I'll get someone to call you
items.form: I'll get someone to call you
items.meaning: Promises to arrange for another person to contact the caller.
items.example: I'm not the right person, but I'll get someone to call you who can help.
items.plain: I will arrange for another person to phone you.
items.note: A common phrase when redirecting a query. Professional and helpful.

items.meaning: Promises to provide the caller's contact information to another person.
items.example: She's not available, but I'll pass your details on so she can call you.
items.plain: I will give your contact information to her.
items.note: A standard phrase when taking a message or facilitating a callback. Neutral.

items.meaning: Promises to verify information and communicate it back to the other person.
items.example: I'm not certain of the exact date, but I'll confirm that with you by email.
items.plain: I will check that information and then tell you it is correct.
items.note: A professional commitment to provide accurate information. Reassuring.

items.meaning: Promises to send a message to help the other person remember something.
items.example: Don't worry about forgetting; I'll send you a reminder closer to the date.
items.plain: I will send you a message to help you remember.
items.note: A helpful and proactive offer, especially for appointments or deadlines. Neutral.

items.meaning: States the time or date when one will be free to take calls or meet.
items.example: I'm in meetings until noon, but I'll be available from 1 PM onwards.
items.plain: I will be free to talk or meet starting at this time.
items.note: A clear and professional way to communicate one's availability. Common.

items.meaning: Informs that one will not be at work or reachable, usually for a period of time.
items.example: Just so you know, I'll be out of office next week with limited access to email.
items.plain: I will not be at work or reachable next week.
items.note: A standard professional phrase for informing others of absence. Clear.

items.text: I'll be back in the office
items.form: I'll be back in the office
items.meaning: States the time or date when one will return to work and be available.
items.example: I'm away until Monday, but I'll be back in the office then.
items.plain: I will return to work at the office on that specific day.
items.note: A common phrase for informing others of one's return from absence. Neutral.

items.text: I'll get straight to the point
items.form: I'll get straight to the point
items.meaning: Promises to be direct and concise, avoiding unnecessary preamble.
items.example: I know you're busy, so I'll get straight to the point about the urgent matter.
items.plain: I will discuss the main topic immediately without delay.
items.note: A professional and efficient opening, showing respect for the other person's time.

items.meaning: States the intention to attempt contact again at a subsequent time.
items.example: Since she's unavailable now, I'll try again later this afternoon.
items.plain: I will attempt to contact her at a different time.
items.note: A common and polite way to handle an unsuccessful attempt to reach someone. Neutral.

items.meaning: Promises to make a phone call to the other person.
items.example: I'll give you a ring tomorrow morning to discuss the details.
items.plain: I will phone you tomorrow morning.
items.note: Informal and friendly, common in British English. Less formal than 'call you'.

items.meaning: Promises to send a short message via mobile phone.
items.example: I'm heading out now, so I'll drop you a text when I arrive.
items.plain: I will send you a text message.
items.note: Informal and common, especially for quick updates or personal communication.

items.meaning: Promises to contact the other person very soon.
items.example: Thanks for the information; I'll be in touch shortly with an update.
items.plain: I will contact you again very soon.
items.note: A polite and professional way to promise a quick follow-up. Common.

items.text: I'll get back to my desk
items.form: I'll get back to my desk
items.meaning: Indicates one is returning to their workspace, often to perform a task.
items.example: I'm just stepping away for a moment, but I'll get back to my desk to send that email.
items.plain: I will return to my work area.
items.note: A common phrase in a professional context, implying a return to work tasks.

items.meaning: The sound is not clear or good, making it hard to hear or be heard.
items.example: We're experiencing poor audio quality on this call; can you hear me clearly?
items.plain: The sound on this call is bad; can you hear me?
items.note: A common way to describe sound problems, suitable for professional settings.

items.meaning: Speech that is unclear and difficult to hear, as if blocked.
items.example: I'm afraid I'm hearing a muffled voice; could you speak closer to the microphone?
items.plain: Your speech is unclear; please speak closer to the microphone.
items.note: A polite way to describe unclear speech, suggesting a microphone adjustment.

items.meaning: The visual transmission is not smooth, appearing to jump or skip frames.
items.example: The choppy video feed is making it difficult to see your screen share clearly.
items.plain: Your video is not smooth, so I can't see your screen share well.
items.note: Describes a common video call problem; polite and descriptive.

items.meaning: A clear lag between speaking and hearing, causing awkward pauses.
items.example: There's a noticeable delay, so let's try to pause briefly after each speaker.
items.plain: There's a lag, so let's pause after each speaker.
items.note: A gentle way to acknowledge latency, suggesting a solution for turn-taking.

items.meaning: Audio quality that is poor, making voices or sounds unclear and unnatural.
items.example: I'm finding the distorted sound makes it hard to understand your words.
items.plain: The unclear sound makes it hard to understand you.
items.note: A precise way to describe poor audio quality, indicating a technical issue.

items.meaning: Asking the other person to say something again because it wasn't heard or understood.
items.example: Sorry, the connection dropped for a second; could you repeat that please?
items.plain: I missed what you said; please say it again.
items.note: A standard, polite request for repetition, suitable for any formal or informal context.

items.meaning: I didn't fully hear or understand what you just said.
items.example: The audio cut out for a moment, so I didn't quite catch that last point.
items.plain: I didn't hear your last point because the audio cut out.
items.note: A polite and common way to indicate you missed part of the conversation.

items.text: let's switch to a phone call
items.form: let's switch to a phone call
items.meaning: Suggesting moving from a video call to an audio-only call due to technical issues.
items.example: Given the persistent video issues, perhaps let's switch to a phone call instead.
items.plain: The video problems are ongoing, so maybe we should just use the phone.
items.note: A practical suggestion when video quality is poor, implying better audio.

items.meaning: My microphone is turned off, so you cannot hear me.
items.example: Oh, apologies, my microphone is muted; I was talking to myself there.
items.plain: Sorry, my microphone is off; I was speaking but you couldn't hear.
items.note: A common self-correction in video calls, often said with a slight chuckle.

items.meaning: Your microphone is turned off, so we cannot hear you.
items.example: Just a quick heads-up, I think you're on mute, as we can't hear you.
items.plain: We can't hear you; your microphone is off.
items.note: A common, polite way to inform someone their microphone is off.

items.meaning: To politely and quickly interrupt to add a point.
items.example: If I may briefly interject, I think we should also consider the budget implications.
items.plain: If I can interrupt quickly, we should consider the budget.
items.note: A formal and polite way to add a point, often used in professional settings.

items.meaning: To provide more details or further explain a previous point.
items.example: I'd like to further elaborate on that point regarding our initial findings.
items.plain: I want to give more details about our initial findings.
items.note: Used when expanding on a point, often after someone else has mentioned it.

items.meaning: To refer back to something previously said by another person and discuss it further.
items.example: I wanted to revisit a point you made earlier about the project timeline.
items.plain: I want to discuss your earlier comment about the project timeline.
items.note: A polite way to bring a previous point back into discussion.

items.meaning: To ask for more specific information or confirm understanding of a point.
items.example: Just to clarify, are we talking about the first quarter or the second?
items.plain: I want to confirm if we mean the first or second quarter.
items.note: Used to seek precision or ensure mutual understanding.

items.meaning: Signalling that you are not in a rush and can let the other person finish speaking.
items.example: No worries, I'm happy to wait until you've finished your thought.
items.plain: It's fine, I can wait for you to finish speaking.
items.note: A polite and accommodating phrase, showing respect for the other speaker.

items.meaning: I will keep my idea or comment to myself for now and share it later.
items.example: You seem to be on a roll, so I'll hold my thought until you're done.
items.plain: You're speaking well, so I'll save my idea for later.
items.note: Indicates a willingness to defer to the current speaker, showing politeness.

items.meaning: A polite way to ask for someone's attention or to speak when they are free.
items.example: When you have a moment, I'd like to discuss the upcoming presentation.
items.plain: When you are free, I want to discuss the presentation.
items.note: A gentle way to request attention without interrupting immediately.

items.meaning: Signalling that you are done speaking or have paused, and the other person can resume.
items.example: That's all I wanted to say for now, so I'll let you continue.
items.plain: I'm done speaking, so you can keep talking.
items.note: A polite way to hand over the conversational floor.

items.text: I just wanted to chime in
items.form: I just wanted to chime in
items.meaning: To add a quick comment or opinion to a conversation.
items.example: I just wanted to chime in and say I agree with your assessment.
items.plain: I wanted to add that I agree with you.
items.note: A slightly informal but common way to contribute to a discussion.

items.meaning: I am ready and eager to listen to what you have to say.
items.example: Go ahead with your proposal; I'm all ears and ready to hear it.
items.plain: Tell me your proposal; I'm ready to listen.
items.note: An idiomatic expression indicating keen attention, suitable for informal to semi-formal.

items.meaning: I believe we have successfully completed our discussion or achieved our goal.
items.example: I think we're good here; all my questions have been answered.
items.plain: I think we're done; all my questions are answered.
items.note: A casual but clear way to signal the end of a specific topic or the call itself.

items.meaning: I will send an email or message summarizing our discussion or next steps.
items.example: To ensure we're aligned, I'll send a follow-up email with the key decisions.
items.plain: I'll email a summary of our decisions to make sure we agree.
items.note: A common professional closing, indicating concrete next steps.

items.meaning: I will provide you with frequent information on the progress or developments.
items.example: I'll update you regularly on the project's status as soon as I have more information.
items.plain: I'll give you regular updates on the project's status when I have more information.
items.note: A clear and professional way to promise ongoing communication.

items.meaning: I believe we have discussed all necessary points and nothing important was missed.
items.example: I think that covers it for today's agenda; thank you for your input.
items.plain: I believe we discussed everything on the agenda today.
items.note: A polite way to conclude a discussion, often inviting others to add anything missed.

items.meaning: I will end the call so you can continue with your other tasks or activities.
items.example: Well, I'll let you get on with your busy schedule now.
items.plain: I'll end the call so you can do your other work.
items.note: A polite and considerate way to end a call, especially if the other person is busy.

items.meaning: Expressing enjoyment or satisfaction from the conversation.
items.example: Thank you for your insights; it was a pleasure speaking with you today.
items.plain: Thank you for your insights; I enjoyed talking with you today.
items.note: A formal and polite closing, suitable for professional interactions.

items.meaning: I will contact you again soon, usually by phone or email.
items.example: Thanks for the update; I'll reach out to you next week regarding the proposal.
items.plain: Thank you; I will contact you next week about the proposal.
items.note: A common, slightly more modern alternative to "I'll be in touch", indicating future communication.

items.meaning: Suggesting that the group or individuals meet again the following week.
items.example: We've made good progress, so let's reconvene next week to finalize the plan.
items.plain: We've done well, so let's meet again next week to finish the plan.
items.note: A formal and efficient way to schedule the next meeting.

items.meaning: I will quickly write down or remember the information you just provided.
items.example: Thank you for the details; I'll jot that down for the report.
items.plain: Thanks for the details; I'll write them down for the report.
items.note: A slightly more informal but common way to say you'll record information.

items.meaning: I will contact you again later with an answer or more information.
items.example: I don't have that information right now, but I'll get back to you by end of day.
items.plain: I don't know now, but I will contact you with the information later today.
items.note: A standard, polite way to promise a future response.

items.meaning: Stating the reason for your phone call.
items.example: Hi, this is Sarah from Acme Corp; I'm calling about the recent invoice.
items.plain: Hello, this is Sarah; I'm calling because of the invoice.
items.note: A very common and direct way to state the purpose of a call.

items.meaning: Asking someone to write down and deliver a message to another person.
items.example: Since he's not available, could you take a message for Mr. Henderson?
items.plain: He's not here, so please write down a message for him.
items.note: A polite and standard way to ask someone to relay information.

items.meaning: I will deliver your communication to the intended recipient.
items.example: Yes, I'll pass on your message to her as soon as she returns to her desk.
items.plain: I will give her your message when she's back at her desk.
items.note: A common and reassuring phrase, confirming the message will be delivered.

items.meaning: I am calling you back because you previously called me.
items.example: Hi Mark, I'm returning your call regarding the project update.
items.plain: Hello Mark, you called me earlier, and I'm calling you back about the project.
items.note: A standard and polite opening when calling someone back.

items.meaning: I will attempt to contact the person or people by phone at a subsequent time.
items.example: They're not answering, so I'll try them again later this afternoon.
items.plain: They're not picking up, so I'll call them later today.
items.note: A common and practical phrase when someone is unavailable.

items.meaning: I will send an email to the person or people.
items.example: Since I can't reach them by phone, I'll drop them an email instead.
items.plain: I can't reach them by phone, so I'll send an email.
items.note: A common, slightly informal but widely accepted way to say "send an email".

items.meaning: I will phone the person or people.
items.example: I need to confirm the details, so I'll give them a call shortly.
items.plain: I need to confirm the details, so I'll phone them soon.
items.note: A common and straightforward way to say you will make a phone call.

items.text: I'll be sure to tell her
items.form: I'll be sure to tell her
items.meaning: I will definitely inform her of your message or request.
items.example: Don't worry, I'll be sure to tell her you called about the meeting.
items.plain: I will definitely tell her you called about the meeting.
items.note: A reassuring phrase, emphasizing certainty that the message will be delivered.

items.meaning: I am calling to see how things are going or to get an update.
items.example: Hi, I'm just checking in to see if you received my previous email.
items.plain: Hello, I'm calling to see if you got my email.
items.note: A common, friendly way to initiate a call, often for a quick update.

items.meaning: I will arrange for the person or people to phone you.
items.example: He's in a meeting right now, but I'll have them call you back.
items.plain: He's busy, but I'll arrange for him to call you back.
items.note: A common phrase used by receptionists or assistants to promise a return call.

items.meaning: Indicates that there are technical issues affecting the call or video conference.
items.example: We seem to be experiencing some technical difficulties with the platform today.
items.plain: It looks like we are having some technical problems with the platform today.
items.note: A polite, slightly formal way to acknowledge a problem, often used in professional settings.

items.text: I'm getting a lot of static
items.form: I'm getting a lot of static
items.meaning: Describes poor audio quality where there is a crackling or hissing sound.
items.example: I'm getting a lot of static on my end, making it hard to hear you clearly.
items.plain: There's a lot of noise on the line, so I can't hear you well.
items.note: Common for phone calls, less so for video calls unless the audio is very poor.

items.text: The video is lagging a bit
items.form: The video is lagging a bit
items.meaning: Explains that the video feed is not smooth and is experiencing delays.
items.example: The video is lagging a bit, so your movements appear jerky on my screen.
items.plain: Your video is delayed and not moving smoothly on my screen.
items.note: A common, informal way to describe video synchronization issues.

items.text: It's a bit difficult to make out
items.form: It's a bit difficult to make out
items.meaning: Expresses that the speaker is having trouble understanding what is being said due to poor audio.
items.example: It's a bit difficult to make out what you're saying with all the background noise.
items.plain: I can't understand you well because of the noise in the background.
items.note: A polite and slightly indirect way to indicate poor comprehension.

items.meaning: States that there are problems with the internet or network connection.
items.example: We're having some connectivity issues, so I might drop off the call unexpectedly.
items.plain: Our internet connection is bad, so I might get disconnected from the call.
items.note: A professional and common way to describe general network problems.

items.text: I'm afraid I can't quite make you out
items.form: I'm afraid I can't quite make you out
items.meaning: Politely states that the speaker cannot understand what the other person is saying.
items.example: I'm afraid I can't quite make you out; the sound quality is very poor.
items.plain: I can't understand you because the sound quality is bad.
items.note: A polite and common expression, often used when the audio is muffled or unclear.

items.meaning: Indicates that the speaker can hear their own voice or other sounds repeating back to them.
items.example: I'm getting an echo on my end, which is making it hard to concentrate.
items.plain: I can hear my own voice repeating, and it's distracting.
items.note: A direct and common way to report a specific audio problem.

items.meaning: Describes a situation where the visual display on the speaker's device is stuck.
items.example: My screen is frozen, so I can't see the presentation slides anymore.
items.plain: The image on my computer is stuck, and I can't see the slides.
items.note: A common and direct way to describe a visual technical issue.

items.text: The audio is cutting in and out
items.form: The audio is cutting in and out
items.meaning: Describes sound that is not continuous, repeatedly stopping and starting.
items.example: The audio is cutting in and out, so I'm missing parts of what you're saying.
items.plain: The sound keeps stopping and starting, so I'm not hearing everything.
items.note: A very common and direct way to describe an unstable audio connection.

items.text: If I may offer a thought
items.form: If I may offer a thought
items.meaning: A polite way to ask for permission to share an idea or opinion.
items.example: If I may offer a thought, perhaps we should consider an alternative approach.
items.plain: Can I share an idea? Maybe we should think about a different way.
items.note: A very polite and slightly formal way to introduce a contribution.

items.meaning: Expresses a desire to make a short remark or observation.
items.example: I'd like to briefly comment on the last point before we move on.
items.plain: I want to say something short about the last topic before we continue.
items.note: A polite and professional way to signal an upcoming short contribution.

items.meaning: Used to check comprehension before responding or continuing.
items.example: If I understand correctly, you're suggesting we postpone the decision until next week.
items.plain: So, you mean we should delay the decision until next week, right?
items.note: A common and useful phrase for clarifying information and ensuring alignment.

items.text: Just to make sure I'm following
items.form: Just to make sure I'm following
items.meaning: Indicates a need to confirm understanding of the discussion so far.
items.example: Just to make sure I'm following, are we still on track for the original deadline?
items.plain: To confirm I understand, is the original deadline still valid?
items.note: A polite and collaborative way to seek clarification during a conversation.

items.meaning: States an intention to save questions for a later time in the discussion.
items.example: I'll hold my questions until the end of your presentation, if that's alright.
items.plain: I will ask my questions after your presentation, if that's okay.
items.note: A polite way to manage turn-taking and avoid interruptions.

items.text: I just wanted to underscore that
items.form: I just wanted to underscore that
items.meaning: Used to emphasize a point that has already been made.
items.example: I just wanted to underscore that the budget constraints are quite strict this quarter.
items.plain: I wanted to emphasize that the budget limits are very strict this quarter.
items.note: A slightly formal and emphatic way to highlight an important point.

items.meaning: Used to repeat or summarize a previous statement for emphasis or clarity.
items.example: To reiterate what you said, the main challenge is indeed resource allocation.
items.plain: As you mentioned, the biggest problem is definitely how we distribute resources.
items.note: A formal and clear way to confirm understanding or reinforce a point.

items.text: I'd like to echo that sentiment
items.form: I'd like to echo that sentiment
items.meaning: Expresses agreement with a feeling or opinion that someone else has stated.
items.example: I'd like to echo that sentiment; teamwork is crucial for this project's success.
items.plain: I agree with that feeling; working together is essential for this project.
items.note: A polite and slightly formal way to express strong agreement.

items.text: If I could just add a quick point
items.form: If I could just add a quick point
items.meaning: A polite way to ask for permission to insert a brief additional comment.
items.example: If I could just add a quick point, the client feedback was overwhelmingly positive.
items.plain: Can I quickly add that the client's feedback was very good?
items.note: A common and polite way to interject briefly without disrupting the flow too much.

items.meaning: Indicates that one trusts and respects another person's specialized knowledge on a topic.
items.example: I'll defer to your expertise on the technical specifications for this new software.
items.plain: I will let you decide on the technical details for this new software because you know more.
items.note: A very polite and professional way to acknowledge someone's superior knowledge.

items.text: To bring things to a close
items.form: To bring things to a close
items.meaning: Used to signal that the discussion or meeting is about to end.
items.example: To bring things to a close, I think we've made good progress today.
items.plain: To finish up, I believe we achieved a lot today.
items.note: A formal and clear way to transition to the end of a conversation.

items.text: It was good to touch base
items.form: It was good to touch base
items.meaning: Expresses that it was productive or pleasant to briefly connect and discuss things.
items.example: It was good to touch base about the project updates; I feel much clearer now.
items.plain: It was helpful to talk briefly about the project updates; I understand better now.
items.note: A common and friendly way to acknowledge a useful short conversation.

items.meaning: Suggests arranging another meeting or call to continue the discussion or review progress.
items.example: Let's schedule a follow-up for next week to review the initial results.
items.plain: We should plan another meeting next week to check the first results.
items.note: A common and practical way to ensure continuity in a project or discussion.

items.meaning: Expresses gratitude for valuable ideas, perspectives, or understanding shared.
items.example: I appreciate your insights on the market trends; they were very helpful.
items.plain: Thank you for your valuable ideas about market trends; they helped a lot.
items.note: A polite and professional way to thank someone for their contribution.

items.text: I think that concludes our discussion
items.form: I think that concludes our discussion
items.meaning: A formal way to state that the conversation or meeting has reached its end.
items.example: I think that concludes our discussion for today, unless anyone has further points.
items.plain: I believe we are finished talking for today, unless there's anything else.
items.note: A formal and definitive way to close a meeting or conversation.

items.text: We've reached the end of our allotted time
items.form: We've reached the end of our allotted time
items.meaning: States that the scheduled duration for the call or meeting has finished.
items.example: We've reached the end of our allotted time, so I'll have to let you go now.
items.plain: Our scheduled time is up, so I need to end the call.
items.note: A polite and professional way to end a call when time is limited.

items.meaning: Describes the conversation as having achieved good results or progress.
items.example: It was a productive call; we managed to resolve several key issues.
items.plain: The call was useful; we solved many important problems.
items.note: A common and positive way to summarize the outcome of a conversation.

items.text: I'll revert to you on that
items.form: I'll revert to you on that
items.meaning: Promises to get back to the person with information or a response.
items.example: I'll revert to you on that budget query once I've spoken to finance.
items.plain: I will get back to you about the budget question after I talk to finance.
items.note: Common in British English, slightly formal. Means "I'll get back to you".

items.text: I'll keep you in the loop
items.form: I'll keep you in the loop
items.meaning: Promises to regularly update someone with information about a situation or project.
items.example: I'll keep you in the loop regarding any developments with the new client proposal.
items.plain: I will regularly inform you about any news concerning the new client proposal.
items.note: A common and friendly idiom, implying ongoing communication.

items.meaning: States that the caller is making the call for another person or organization.
items.example: I'm calling on behalf of Mr. Smith regarding the outstanding invoice.
items.plain: I am calling for Mr. Smith about the unpaid bill.
items.note: A formal and professional way to introduce the purpose of a call.

items.text: Could you ask them to call me back
items.form: Could you ask them to call me back
items.meaning: A polite request for someone to relay a message for a return call.
items.example: Could you ask them to call me back when they have a moment?
items.plain: Please tell them to phone me back when they are free.
items.note: A common and polite way to leave a message requesting a return call.

items.meaning: States an intention to provide phone number, email, or other ways to be reached.
items.example: I'll leave my contact details with your assistant so they can reach me.
items.plain: I will give your assistant my phone number and email so they can contact me.
items.note: A practical and common phrase when leaving a message.

items.text: Please let them know I called
items.form: Please let them know I called
items.meaning: A polite request to inform someone that the caller attempted to reach them.
items.example: Please let them know I called about the meeting next Tuesday.
items.plain: Tell them that I phoned about the meeting next Tuesday.
items.note: A very common and simple way to leave a message.

items.text: I'll follow up with them directly
items.form: I'll follow up with them directly
items.meaning: States an intention to contact the person concerned without an intermediary.
items.example: I'll follow up with them directly if I don't hear back by tomorrow afternoon.
items.plain: I will contact them myself if they don't reply by tomorrow afternoon.
items.note: A professional way to indicate taking personal responsibility for communication.

items.meaning: Promises to provide advance notice or a warning about something.
items.example: I'll give them a heads-up that you'll be calling about the proposal.
items.plain: I will tell them in advance that you will call about the proposal.
items.note: A common and informal idiom for providing a pre-notification.

items.text: I'll ask them to get back to you
items.form: I'll ask them to get back to you
items.meaning: Promises to request that the person you're trying to reach returns your call or message.
items.example: I'll ask them to get back to you as soon as they're available.
items.plain: I will tell them to contact you when they are free.
items.note: A common and polite way to assure someone their message will be acted upon.

items.meaning: Promises to inform someone about a specific piece of information.
items.example: I'll make sure they're aware of the updated delivery schedule.
items.plain: I will ensure they know about the new delivery schedule.
items.note: A professional and reassuring way to confirm information will be passed on.

items.meaning: Promises to communicate the exact content of a message to the intended recipient.
items.example: I'll convey your message to the team leader as soon as she returns.
items.plain: I will give your message to the team leader when she comes back.
items.note: A formal and precise way to promise to pass on information.

items.text: I'll get back to you with an answer
items.form: I'll get back to you with an answer
items.meaning: Promises to provide a response or solution after finding out the necessary information.
items.example: I'll get back to you with an answer about the project timeline by end of day.
items.plain: I will reply to you with information about the project timeline by the end of the day.
items.note: A common and professional way to commit to providing a specific response.
